# Lazzat Marketing

Master marketing memory for Lazzat Grill & Shakes. Use this skill any time a task touches Lazzat
brand, menu, audience, competitors, content, social growth, website claims, or strategy.

**Not in this skill:** full animated-series bible/craft. For mascot series / episode production,
use the separate animated-series skill (`New Stories/animated_series/`). A short creative pointer
lives in `references/09-current-state-roadmap.md`.

Read `references/00-INDEX.md` first, then open only the file(s) needed for the current task.
Do not load every file for every task.

- Never say **"charcoal."** Say **"lava stone

- Never say **"charcoal."** Say **"lava stone grilling"** (ops moved off charcoal; public PR confirms lava stones).

- Every piece of content should map to one of the six content pillars (`06`).
- Ads launch/reset on **Tuesdays**; same video goes to all platforms simultaneously.

title: 01-brand-identity
text:
# Lazzat Grill & Shakes — Brand Identity

## What It Is
Premium fast-casual grill + shakes restaurant. Brampton, Ontario. Takeaway & delivery.
**Global Canadian brand.** Never Pakistani, South Asian, or Desi in positioning.
Public product framing: flame-grilled bowls, real-fruit shakes, skewers over live fire.

Internal note: meat is clean/ethically sourced (ops: Australia/NZ sourced). Do **not** say "halal" in customer-facing copy.

## Motto / Tagline Hierarchy (locked)

| Priority | Line | Where to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary (brand / campaigns)** | "Taste the World. Crafted Fresh. Served Fast." | Strategy docs, brand decks, campaign headers |
| **Secondary** | "Uniting Through Flavours." | Pinterest, soft brand / culture-unity posts |
| **Website hero (public)** | "Flame-Grilled Bowls. Real-Fruit Shakes." | lazzat.ca homepage, web-matched ads |
| **Creative / video (optional)** | "Crafted to Perfection" · "Every feast begins here" · "Real Flavor, Real Freshness" | AI video /

title: 01-brand-identity (part 2)
text:
/ video (optional)** | "Crafted to Perfection" · "Every feast begins here" · "Real Flavor, Real Freshness" | AI video / lifestyle packs only — see creative pointer in `09`; do not override primary for strategy decks |

## Brand Story
Started with one question: why does fresh, flavorful food take so long, and why does fast food taste bland?
After years running kitchens across Canada, the same problem kept showing up everywhere.
Lazzat (also spelled "Lezzat" in some countries) was built to answer that question.
4 years of testing, failing, refining, rebuilding before launch.
Not a rushed idea. A tested product.

## Meaning of the Name
"Lazzat" means taste, delight, richness in both Punjabi and Urdu.
Instant cultural resonance in Brampton, but the brand itself is positioned as Canadian, not ethnic.

## Goals & Vision (3 core statements — from Complete Marketing Strategy 2026)
1. **Canadian brand** — not Pakistani, not Indian, not Desi. Made for every person in this country.

their culture and their wallet, Lazzat is the only fast-casual restaurant delivering live-flame
global cuisine with complete dietary inclusivity (no pork, no beef, alcohol-free) at honest pricing.

ity Rules
- Canadian brand. Not Pakistani, not Indian, not Desi.
- Target is everyone: young Canada, white Canada, brown Canada, black Canada.
- Ambition level: McDonald's/Chipotle scale thinking, applied to a live-fire global grill concept.

## Language Rules (Non-Negotiable)
| Topic | Never Say | Always Say |
|---|---|---|
| Meat sourcing | Halal | Clean meat, ethically sourced, blood-free preparation |
| Pricing | Cheap, affordable, budget | Honest pricing, premium without the shock price |
| Competitors | Name and shame | "Why pay $50 elsewhere for the same grill?" |
| Speed | Fast food | Fresh. Fast. No compromise. *(tone only — do not invent timed SLA claims)* |
| Cooking method | Charcoal | Lava stone grilling |

- Halal never appears in customer-facing copy (including Google Ads keyword text).
- No religious phrases in brand communications (no "JazakAllah" etc).
- Maple Lodge Farms is the approved reference for clean meat sourcing claims when needed.
- No South Asian / Desi /

## Brand Values Pillars
1. No pork
2. No beef
3. Alcohol-free
4. Vegetarian & vegan options available
5. Respect for all cultures and beliefs simultaneously

## Visual Identity
- Background: dark, near-black, premium feel
- Color accents: warm amber/gold from flame, small red for CTA/energy
- Logo always on black or dark background
- Creative pack hexes (video/lifestyle): Primary Gold `#EAC329`, Light Gold `#F1CF4D`, Deep Gold `#8A8A3E`, Midnight Black `#0D0D0D`, Cream `#FAF7F0`
- Typography (creative pack): Headings Rallomy/Satisfy · Sub Minion/Playfair · Body Montserrat — marketing decks may use bold sans for launch materials
- Photography: char marks, steam, sauce drizzle, cut interior visible = trust signals
- Never flat-lay on white background (reads as delivery-app photography, not brand photography)

## Key Differentiators (Unique Strengths)
- **Lava stone grilling** (replaced real charcoal), marketed as eco-friendly innovation — never called "charcoal" in copy
- Australia/NZ clean-sourced meat, no frozen meat *(ops claim — confirm before hard guarantees)*, taste-test narrative: 95% rated extremely tender/juicy/pink
- Himalayan pink salt counter, ~600-million-year-old stone, internally lit, built-in photo prop
- 4–5 unique tangy salads (pickled onion style, not creamy); small platter includes 1 free salad
- Big platters = primary revenue driver
- 11 years experience managing 20+ restaurants (approved claim)
- No pork, no alcohol
- Build-your-own-plate: protein + sauce + side, vegan/GF builds available
- Global menu spanning 5+ cuisines in one place: Sajji, Biryani, Doner, Skewers, Paneer Tikka
- Dual pillar: serious grill + real-fruit shakes under one brand

## Locked Marketing Rules
- Never invent timed freshness SLAs ("5-minute fresh"), blanket allergen-free, or unverified "zero frozen" claims until ops confirms
- Website may use **real-fruit shakes**, **salads by hand**, **skewers over live fire** — see `10-website-public-lock.md`
- Never use "Pakistani," "South Asian," or "Desi"
- Never use religious phrases in brand comms
- Ads always launch/reset on Tuesdays
- All platforms receive the same video simultaneously
- Content formula: 1 confirmed strength + 1 menu item per week
- TikTok managed from Canadian IP only

# Lazzat — Locations, Contact, Team

## Locations

### Location 1 — OPEN: McVean Dr (Castlemore / North-East Brampton)
Address: **11685 McVean Dr, Brampton, ON L6P 4N5**
Area profile: Premium, affluent Punjabi Sikh + Gujarati Hindu + Pakistani families
Household income: $111K+ median, many above $150K in Castlemore
Hours (ops brain): Mon–Thu 11am–11pm, Fri–Sat 11am–12am, Sun 12pm–10pm
Public/PR note (INsauga Jun 2026): listed as open daily 11am–11pm — prefer **ops hours above** for staff/systems; reconcile NAP on GMB if they differ.
Features: Parking available, Free WiFi, **Takeaway only**
Best menu items to push here: Lamb Chops, Chicken Sajji, Biryani, Lamb Skewers
Marketing angle: Premium grill, family occasion dining

### Location 2 — Clarence St (Downtown Brampton)

# Lazzat — Full Menu Reference

Note: Prices below are from internal menu data export (shown in GBP in source file in some exports —
treat as **placeholder structure**, not final CAD pricing). Use for item names, descriptions,
pairings, and category structure. Confirm live CAD prices on Toast / delivery apps / site before
publishing price claims.

## Public website framing (lazzat.ca)
Public site positions Lazzat as: **flame-grilled bowls + real-fruit shakes**; skewers (one, two, or three);
salads by hand; shakes to order. Press also mentions wraps, family platters, bowl+shake combos.
Use `10-website-public-lock.md` for public claim language. This file remains the **internal full catalogue**.

title: 04-brampton-demographics-audience
text:
# Brampton Demographics & Target Audience

## Brampton Snapshot (2026)
Population: ~833,000 (2026 projection), growth rate 2.58% annually, Canada's fastest growing city.
Median age: 35.8 years. Average household size: 3.6 (vs 2.5 national avg).
Median household income: $111,000.
Foreign-born residents: 52.9%.
Visible minorities: 80.6% of population.

## Ethnicity Breakdown
- South Asian: ~48-52% of Brampton (dominant group)
  - Punjabi/Sikh: largest sub-group (~163,000 Sikhs)
  - Gujarati Hindu: 3.4% mother tongue
  - Pakistani (Urdu-speaking): 20,400+ residents
- Black/Caribbean: ~13-13.5% (Jamaican 22,200, Guyanese 13,900, Trinidadian 7,400)
- Filipino: 15,300
- Sri Lankan Tamil: 12,300
- European/White: 18.9%

## Religion in Brampton (2021 Census)
- Christianity: 35.7%
- Sikhism: 25.1% (HIGHEST of any city in Canada)
- Hinduism: 18.1%
- Islam: 9.1%
- No Religion: 10.3%

Critical insight: Sikh + Hindu + Muslim = 52.3% of Brampton. All three avoid pork, beef, and alcohol.

Critical insight: Sikh + Hindu + Muslim = 52.3% of Brampton. All three avoid pork, beef, and alcohol.
Lazzat's menu serves all three simultaneously with zero friction.

## Languages
Mother tongue: English 42.9%, Punjabi 21.7% (2nd language of the city), Gujarati 3.4%, Urdu 3.4%, Hindi 3.0%.
Punjabi as a second language at this scale is unmatched by any other Canadian city.

## Target Audience Rules (Locked)
- Radius: 3km around both locations
- Priority age: Millennials and Gen Z
- Language targeting: English, Punjabi, Urdu, Arabic
- Exclude general Hindu via negative targeting (per brand instruction)
- Target residents not visited in 4+ hours (location/behavior targeting)
- Big family platter buyers as a priority segment
- Follower/lookalike lists: unknown people only, never friends lists

## Four Buyer Personas

### 1. Punjabi/Sikh Family (Castlemore, Gore)
Household 4-6, income $111K+, weekend family dining, loves grill culture, biryani, seekh kabab.
Pain point: can't

text:

Household 4-6, income $111K+, weekend family dining, loves grill culture, biryani, seekh kabab.
Pain point: can't find premium grill without alcohol or pork risk.
Best content: Friday/weekend posts, Vaisakhi campaign, Punjabi-language captions, Lamb + Sajji reels.

### 2. Pakistani/Muslim Family (Bramalea, Downtown)
20,400+ community, biryani and sajji are comfort foods, family group dining.
Pain point: uncertainty about meat sourcing trust.
Best content: Eid content, Urdu/English captions, biryani + sajji close-ups, clean meat trust posts.

### 3. Gujarati/Hindu Family (Bramalea, Clarence St)
Vegetarian-leaning, Diwali/Navratri celebrators, no beef non-negotiable.
Pain point: most BBQ places have no real vegetarian option.
Best content: Paneer Tikka reels, Diwali/Navratri content, vegetarian spotlight posts.

### 4. Second-Gen & Young Professional (all areas, 18-34)
Canadian-born, Instagram/TikTok native, food-curious, values aesthetics.
Pain point: wants cultural roots but

Canadian-born, Instagram/TikTok native, food-curious, values aesthetics.
Pain point: wants cultural roots but not a dated experience.
Best content: Reels, TikTok, dessert/shake content, hook-based viral formats, BTS.

## Neighbourhood Notes
- Castlemore/Vales of Castlemore (North-East, near McVean Dr): premium, affluent Punjabi Sikh + Gujarati Hindu + Pakistani. Large families, high disposable income.
- Clarence St / Queen St Corridor (near Location 2): older buildings, affordable, high foot traffic, Jamaican/Caribbean + South Asian + European mix.
- Bramalea: South Asian dominant, Caribbean mix, budget-conscious families, strong community feel.
- Gore Meadows: newest development, new immigrant families, fast growing.

## Consumer Psychology Notes
- Word-of-mouth and community WhatsApp/Facebook groups drive decisions more than ads.
- Food = cultural identity for 1st/2nd gen immigrants. A brand that "gets their culture" earns loyalty.
- Family dining is the primary occasion

# Cultural Calendar & Campaign Hooks (Brampton)

| Month | Occasion | Target Community | Campaign Idea | Hero Dish |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| April | Vaisakhi (Sikh New Year) | Punjabi Sikh, 163K in Brampton | Family feast package, Punjabi-language caption | Chicken Skewers + Lamb Seekh |
| May/Jun | Eid ul-Fitr | Muslim community, 20,400+ | Family bundle offer, clean meat messaging front and centre | Biryani + Chicken Sajji |
| Jun/Jul | Eid ul-Adha (Bakra Eid) | Muslim community, lamb-forward | Lamb week campaign, "the lamb you've been waiting for" | Lamb Chops + Lamb Seekh |
| Jul/Aug | Caribbean Carnival / JAMBANA | Jamaican + Caribbean, 40K+ | Bold sauces, BBQ wraps, Doner focus, Clarence St hero content | Doner + Smoked Chicken Wrap |
| Sep/Oct | Navratri | Gujarati Hindu families | Vegetarian spotlight week, Paneer Tikka as hero | Paneer Tikka + Grilled Veg |
| Oct/Nov | Diwali | Hindu + Sikh, largest South Asian occasion | Diwali family feast, premium platter, warm golden

title: 05-cultural-calendar-campaigns (part 2)
text:
eg |
| Oct/Nov | Diwali | Hindu + Sikh, largest South Asian occasion | Diwali family feast, premium platter, warm golden visuals | Full menu, family platter |
| Nov | Guru Nanak Gurpurab | Sikh community | Community gratitude post, no hard sell | Chicken Seekh Kabab |
| Dec | Christmas/New Year | Filipino Catholic + Caribbean | Holiday feast campaign, dessert upsell | Sajji + Dessert selection |

## Quarterly Themes
- Q2 (Apr-Jun): Vaisakhi, Ramadan tail-end, Eid ul-Fitr
- Q3 (Jul-Sep): Summer BBQ, Caribbean Carnival, patio season content
- Q4 (Oct-Dec): Navratri, Diwali, Gurpurab, Christmas/New Year

## Rule
Plan campaign content at least 2 weeks before each occasion. These are the highest-revenue windows
of the year and are treated as the backbone of the content calendar, not optional add-ons.

title: 06-content-social-strategy
text:
# Content & Social Media Strategy

## Six Content Pillars
1. We Respect Every Table - no pork, no beef, no alcohol, clean meat, every culture welcomed
2. Your Culture, Your Plate - Sajji = Balochi, Biryani = South Asian comfort, Doner = Mediterranean
3. Build Your Own Plate - protein + sauce + side, vegan/GF builds
4. Real Flame. Not Overpriced. - grill visuals, "others charge $40+, we don't," honest pricing story
5. Live Grill Experience - fire/smoke close-ups, char marks forming, raw-to-plated in 60 seconds
6. Speed + Brampton Community - two locations, cultural occasions, family Friday posts

## Weekly Posting Rhythm
- Monday 12-1pm: Photo/Carousel - Pillar 1 or 2 (cultural respect / clean meat messaging)
- Wednesday 6-8pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 4 or 5 (grill footage / price hook)
- Friday 5-7pm: Photo/Carousel - Pillar 3 or 4 (build your plate / family occasion)
- Sunday 6-9pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 2 or 6 (brand story / community)

Content formula: 1 confirmed strength +

title: 06-content-social-strategy (part 2)
text:
ion)
- Sunday 6-9pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 2 or 6 (brand story / community)

Content formula: 1 confirmed strength + 1 menu item per week.
All platforms get the same video simultaneously.
Ads always launch/reset on Tuesdays.

## Visual Rules for Every Post
- Dark, near-black background, food should pop
- Warm amber/gold flame-toned lighting, never cool/clinical
- Always show char marks, sauce drizzle, steam, or cut interior
- Lazzat logo subtle in a bottom corner of every image
- Video always vertical 9:16, always with subtitles (sound-off viewing must work)

## Growth Tactics
- Bill-time follow-and-review discount
- Reel-based coupon codes, extendable to Uber Eats/DoorDash
- Hot sauce challenge ("Wall of the Brave" guerrilla idea — optional)
- Dedicated content creator team model
- Weekly review contest
- Trending audio and keyword capture, adopt new platform features early
- Loyalty: stamp card (8→9th free), birthday %, bring-a-friend (legacy plan — confirm live)
- Weekend "Dish

title: 06-content-social-strategy (part 3)
text:
atures early
- Loyalty: stamp card (8→9th free), birthday %, bring-a-friend (legacy plan — confirm live)
- Weekend "Dish of the Weekend" (announce Thu; Fri–Sun discount)

Full channel inventory + documented growth targets → `11-social-channels-growth.md`.

## Influencer Approach
Direct local Brampton micro-influencer outreach works better than platform-based outreach
(platforms like Collabstr mainly yielded paid-collab requests, not organic fits).
Process: personal DM, no script, complimentary tasting for two, ask to add @lazzat.ca as collaborator
on their reel. Soha handles on-ground hospitality when Usama is remote. Follow-up via WhatsApp.
No cash payment in early phase, food only.

## Opening Special (reference)

Increase visibility in local takeaway searches in Brampton, bring more traffic, more orders.

Every blog must include: a local reference (Brampton, McVean Dr, Clarence St), an FAQ section for
featured snippet eligibility, internal links to menu/ordering pages, optimized image alt text.

# Competitor Intelligence (Clarence St Area)

When writing customer copy from this file: say **lava stone / flame grill**, never "charcoal."
Internal competitor research may still say charcoal historically — translate for public output.

## The Single Biggest Finding
After analyzing 26+ competitors near Clarence St: zero restaurants combine Lava/Flame Grill +
No Pork/Beef/Alcohol + Global Menu + All Delivery Platforms + Active Social Media.
Lazzat owns this lane by default.

## Direct Competitors
### King Tandoori Kennedy
4.0 stars, 7,757+ reviews, 8,137 IG followers. Open 24 hours.
Weakness: HAS FULL ALCOHOL BAR, not halal. Portions shrinking. Plastic found in food (documented).
Lazzat angle: "Every item clean. No alcohol. No confusion."

### Baigs Grill
4.2 stars, 2,047 reviews, 1,192 IG (only 49 posts).
Weakness: Closed Monday AND Tuesday. $452 bad bill complaint. Biryani "tasteless, missing meat." Zero TikTok.
Lazzat angle: Post "WE ARE OPEN" every Mon/Tue. Target disappointed

text:
int. Biryani "tasteless, missing meat." Zero TikTok.
Lazzat angle: Post "WE ARE OPEN" every Mon/Tue. Target disappointed biryani customers.

title: 12-legacy-vs-current-strategy
text:
# Legacy vs Current Strategy

How older decks relate to what this skill uses **now**. Prefer current locks when they conflict.

## Sources reconciled for this skill
1. `lazzat brain now/` (00–09) — primary operating SSOT
2. `Lazzat old Marketing file.pdf` — Canva "Complete Marketing Strategy 2026" (37 pages)
3. `Lazzat Brand Marketing Strategy/` — esp. `Lazzat_Strategy_v3_FINAL.docx`, strengths report, demographics txt
4. Live [lazzat.ca](https://www.lazzat.ca) + INsauga PR (Jun 2026)
5. Creative pointer: workspace `Lazzat_Brain.md` (not expanded here)

## Conflict log → resolution

| Topic | Legacy / old PDF / early docs | Current lock |
|---|---|---|
| Cooking method | "Real charcoal," "only charcoal grill in Brampton," charcoal in SEO titles & ads | **Lava stone grilling** — never say charcoal in customer copy |
| Halal language | "100% Halal," Google keyword "halal food near me" | **Never "halal" in customer-facing copy or ads** — clean meat / ethically sourced |
| Freshness /

title: 12-legacy-vs-current-strategy (part 2)
text:
"halal food near me" | **Never "halal" in customer-facing copy or ads** — clean meat / ethically sourced |
| Freshness / speed | "5-minute fresh promise," heavy freshness guarantees | Tone OK ("Fresh. Fast. No compromise.") — **no timed SLA** until ops confirms |
| Tagline | Taste the World… (strategy) | Keep as **primary**; website hero = Flame-Grilled Bowls…; secondary = Uniting Through Flavours |
| Address Loc1 | Strengths report "Bovaird Drive West" | **11685 McVean Dr** only |
| Mayfield | Announced in press | **Planned only** until ops/GMB confirm |
| IG handle | Guerrilla "tag @lazzatgrill" | **@lazzat.ca** |
| Industry "18/20 solved" | PDF claims Lazzat already solves every industry failure | Treat as **aspiration** — only claim confirmed strengths from `01` + `10` |
| Allergen / zero frozen | Claimed broadly in old PDF | **Do not claim** until Menu Engineer / ops confirm |
| Charcoal in blog titles | Strategy v3 blog list | Rewrite to flame / lava-stone / grill language

title: 12-legacy-vs-current-strategy (part 3)
text:
ineer / ops confirm |
| Charcoal in blog titles | Strategy v3 blog list | Rewrite to flame / lava-stone / grill language (`07`) |
| Visual fonts | Creative pack uses display/serif mix | Marketing decks often bold sans; creative hexes allowed for video |

## What we **kept** from the old Complete Marketing Strategy 2026
- Three core vision statements (Canadian / everyone / world-level)
- Organic-first launch mindset; GMB review obsession
- Six content pillars + Tue ad reset + simultaneous multi-platform posting
- Persona set (Punjabi/Sikh, Pakistani/Muslim, Gujarati/Hindu, second-gen 18–34)
- Cultural calendar backbone
- Dual pillar grill + shakes
- Dietary universality (no pork, no beef, alcohol-free, veg options)
- Agile test-and-double-down framework
- Guerrilla ideas worth keeping as **optional**: pink salt photo wall, sticker wall, Wall of the Brave, visible grill, packaging as media
- Loyalty & WhatsApp database thinking (confirm before promising)
- 2 blogs/week local SEO engine

title: 12-legacy-vs-current-strategy (part 4)
text:
ll, packaging as media
- Loyalty & WhatsApp database thinking (confirm before promising)
- 2 blogs/week local SEO engine
- Micro-influencer tasting model (refined: direct outreach > Collabstr)

## What we **dropped or demoted**
- Charcoal-as-hero messaging
- Halal-as-public-claim / halal ad keywords
- Unverified 5-minute / allergen / zero-frozen guarantees
- Treating all 18–20 "industry solutions" as publishable facts
- Wrong Bovaird address
- @lazzatgrill handle
- Assuming Clarence/Mayfield open without verification
- Inventing follower/review counts from the 6-month roadmap table as if current

## What **supersedes** legacy for day-to-day
| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Voice & claims | `01` + `10` |
| Where we are / pending | `09` |
| Social execution | `06` + `11` |
| Menu facts | `03` |
| Competitor angles | `08` (lava-stone language) |

## Legacy roadmap themes (context only)
Month themes from old PDF: Ignite → Build → Amplify → Dominate → Celebrate → Scale.
Useful for storytelling;

text:

Out of scope for deep detail here. Marketing may reference that creative work exists; production rules live in the animated-series skill / `Lazzat_Brain.md`.

# Lazzat Brain - Index

Complete knowledge base for Lazzat Grill & Shakes marketing work.

1. 01-brand-identity.md - positioning, tagline, story, language rules, visual identity, differentiators
2. 02-locations-team-contact.md - both locations, warehouse, team roles, tools/platforms
3. 03-menu-full.md - full menu, sauces, menu-culture alignment, planned expansion
4. 04-brampton-demographics-audience.md - Brampton stats, personas, targeting rules
5. 05-cultural-calendar-campaigns.md - festival calendar and campaign hooks
6. 06-content-social-strategy.md - content pillars, posting schedule, growth tactics, KPIs
7. 07-seo-strategy.md - blog plan, on-page/off-page SEO, GMB strategy
8. 08-competitor-intelligence.md - direct/partial/indirect competitors, weaknesses, angles
9. 09-current-state-roadmap.md - active workstreams, pending tasks, roadmap, working style notes

Use this folder as the single source of truth for any Lazzat content, strategy, or campaign work.

title: 01-brand-identity
text:
# Lazzat Grill & Shakes - Brand Identity

## What It Is
Premium fast-casual halal grill restaurant. Two Brampton, Ontario locations.
Global Canadian brand. Never Pakistani, South Asian, or Desi in positioning.

## Tagline
"Taste the World. Crafted Fresh. Served Fast."
Also used: "Uniting Through Flavours."

## Brand Story
Started with one question: why does fresh, flavorful food take so long, and why does fast food taste bland?
After years running kitchens across Canada, the same problem kept showing up everywhere.
Lazzat (also spelled "Lezzat" in some countries) was built to answer that question.
4 years of testing, failing, refining, rebuilding before launch.
Not a rushed idea. A tested product.

## Meaning of the Name
"Lazzat" means taste, delight, richness in both Punjabi and Urdu.
Instant cultural resonance in Brampton, but the brand itself is positioned as Canadian, not ethnic.

## Positioning Statement
For families and individuals in Brampton who want premium

title: 01-brand-identity (part 2)
text:
positioned as Canadian, not ethnic.

## Positioning Statement
For families and individuals in Brampton who want premium charcoal/lava-grilled food that respects
their culture and their wallet, Lazzat is the only fast-casual restaurant delivering live-flame
global cuisine with complete dietary inclusivity (no pork, no beef, alcohol-free) at honest pricing.

## Core Identity Rules
- Canadian brand. Not Pakistani, not Indian, not Desi.
- Target is everyone: young Canada, white Canada, brown Canada, black Canada.
- Ambition level: McDonald's/Chipotle scale thinking, applied to a live-fire global grill concept.
- 10-franchise Canada expansion vision (Brampton now, then Mississauga, Toronto, Surrey, Edmonton,
  Calgary, Ottawa, Hamilton, Windsor, Vancouver).

## Language Rules (Non-Negotiable)
| Topic | Never Say | Always Say |
|---|---|---|
| Meat sourcing | Halal | Clean meat, ethically sourced, blood-free preparation |
| Pricing | Cheap, affordable, budget | Honest pricing, premium

title: 01-brand-identity (part 3)
text:
Clean meat, ethically sourced, blood-free preparation |
| Pricing | Cheap, affordable, budget | Honest pricing, premium without the shock price |
| Competitors | Name and shame | "Why pay $50 elsewhere for the same grill?" |
| Speed | Fast food | Fresh. Fast. No compromise. |
| Cooking method | Charcoal | Lava stone grilling |

- Halal never appears in customer-facing copy.
- No religious phrases in brand communications (no "JazakAllah" etc).
- Maple Lodge Farms is the approved reference for clean meat sourcing claims.
- No South Asian / Desi / Pakistani framing anywhere in brand voice.

## Brand Values Pillars
1. No pork
2. No beef
3. Alcohol-free
4. Vegetarian & vegan options available
5. Respect for all cultures and beliefs simultaneously

## Visual Identity
- Background: dark, near-black, premium feel
- Color accents: warm amber/gold from flame, small red for CTA/energy
- Logo always on black or dark background
- Typography: bold sans-serif headlines, no decorative/script fonts
-

title: 01-brand-identity (part 4)
text:
A/energy
- Logo always on black or dark background
- Typography: bold sans-serif headlines, no decorative/script fonts
- Photography: char marks, steam, sauce drizzle, cut interior visible = trust signals
- Never flat-lay on white background (that reads as delivery-app photography, not brand photography)

## Key Differentiators (Unique Strengths)
- Lava stone grilling (replaced real charcoal), marketed as eco-friendly innovation, never called "charcoal" in copy
- Australia/NZ halal-sourced meat, no frozen meat, lower cost than Canadian equivalent with better taste test results (95% rated extremely tender/juicy/pink)
- Himalayan pink salt counter, 600-million-year-old stone, internally lit, built-in photo prop
- 4-5 unique tangy salads (pickled onion style, not creamy), small platter includes 1 free salad
- Big platters = primary revenue driver
- 11 years experience managing 20+ restaurants (approved claim)
- No pork, no alcohol
- Build-your-own-plate: protein + sauce + side, vegan/GF

title: 01-brand-identity (part 5)
text:
managing 20+ restaurants (approved claim)
- No pork, no alcohol
- Build-your-own-plate: protein + sauce + side, vegan/GF builds available
- Global menu spanning 5+ cuisines in one place: Sajji, Biryani, Doner, Skewers, Paneer Tikka

## Locked Marketing Rules
- Never mention speed, freshness, or allergen claims (not operationally confirmed yet)
- Never use "Pakistani," "South Asian," or "Desi"
- Never use religious phrases in brand comms
- Ads always launch/reset on Tuesdays
- All platforms receive the same video simultaneously
- Content formula: 1 confirmed strength + 1 menu item per week
- TikTok managed from Canadian IP only
- All platform access via Octet Solutions company email

# Lazzat - Locations, Contact, Team

## Locations

### Location 1: McVean Dr (Castlemore / North-East Brampton)
Address: 11685 McVean Dr, Brampton, ON L6P 4N5
Area profile: Premium, affluent Punjabi Sikh + Gujarati Hindu + Pakistani families
Household income: $111K+ median, many above $150K in Castlemore
Hours: Mon-Thu 11am-11pm, Fri-Sat 11am-12am, Sun 12pm-10pm
Features: Parking available, Free WiFi, Takeaway only
Best menu items to push here: Lamb Chops, Chicken Sajji, Biryani, Lamb Skewers
Marketing angle: Premium grill, family occasion dining

### Location 2: Clarence St (Downtown Brampton)
Address: 143 Clarence St, Unit 10, Brampton, ON L6W 1T2
Area profile: Mixed diverse community, Jamaican/Caribbean, South Asian, European
Income level: Mid-range, value-conscious but quality-seeking
Hours: Mon-Thu 10am-10pm, Fri-Sat 10am-11pm, Sun 11am-9pm
Features: Parking available, Free WiFi, Takeaway only
Best menu items to push here: Wraps, Doner, Paneer Tikka, Crispy Fries, Shakes

title: 04-brampton-demographics-audience
text:
# Brampton Demographics & Target Audience

## Brampton Snapshot (2026)
Population: ~833,000 (2026 projection), growth rate 2.58% annually, Canada's fastest growing city.
Median age: 35.8 years. Average household size: 3.6 (vs 2.5 national avg).
Median household income: $111,000.
Foreign-born residents: 52.9%.
Visible minorities: 80.6% of population.

## Ethnicity Breakdown
- South Asian: ~48-52% of Brampton (dominant group)
  - Punjabi/Sikh: largest sub-group (~163,000 Sikhs)
  - Gujarati Hindu: 3.4% mother tongue
  - Pakistani (Urdu-speaking): 20,400+ residents
- Black/Caribbean: ~13-13.5% (Jamaican 22,200, Guyanese 13,900, Trinidadian 7,400)
- Filipino: 15,300
- Sri Lankan Tamil: 12,300
- European/White: 18.9%

## Religion in Brampton (2021 Census)
- Christianity: 35.7%
- Sikhism: 25.1% (HIGHEST of any city in Canada)
- Hinduism: 18.1%
- Islam: 9.1%
- No Religion: 10.3%

Critical insight: Sikh + Hindu + Muslim = 52.3% of Brampton. All three avoid pork, beef, and alcohol.

Critical insight: Sikh + Hindu + Muslim = 52.3% of Brampton. All three avoid pork, beef, and alcohol.
Lazzat's menu serves all three simultaneously with zero friction.

## Languages
Mother tongue: English 42.9%, Punjabi 21.7% (2nd language of the city), Gujarati 3.4%, Urdu 3.4%, Hindi 3.0%.
Punjabi as a second language at this scale is unmatched by any other Canadian city.

## Target Audience Rules (Locked)
- Radius: 3km around both locations
- Priority age: Millennials and Gen Z
- Language targeting: English, Punjabi, Urdu, Arabic
- Exclude general Hindu via negative targeting (per brand instruction)
- Target residents not visited in 4+ hours (location/behavior targeting)
- Big family platter buyers as a priority segment
- Follower/lookalike lists: unknown people only, never friends lists

## Four Buyer Personas

### 1. Punjabi/Sikh Family (Castlemore, Gore)
Household 4-6, income $111K+, weekend family dining, loves grill culture, biryani, seekh kabab.

Household 4-6, income $111K+, weekend family dining, loves grill culture, biryani, seekh kabab.
Pain point: can't find premium grill without alcohol or pork risk.
Best content: Friday/weekend posts, Vaisakhi campaign, Punjabi-language captions, Lamb + Sajji reels.

### 2. Pakistani/Muslim Family (Bramalea, Downtown)
20,400+ community, biryani and sajji are comfort foods, family group dining.
Pain point: uncertainty about meat sourcing trust.
Best content: Eid content, Urdu/English captions, biryani + sajji close-ups, clean meat trust posts.

### 3. Gujarati/Hindu Family (Bramalea, Clarence St)
Vegetarian-leaning, Diwali/Navratri celebrators, no beef non-negotiable.
Pain point: most BBQ places have no real vegetarian option.
Best content: Paneer Tikka reels, Diwali/Navratri content, vegetarian spotlight posts.

## Neighbourhood Notes
- Castlemore/Vales of Castlemore (North-East, near McVean Dr): premium, affluent Punjabi Sikh + Gujarati Hindu + Pakistani. Large families, high disposable income.
- Clarence St / Queen St Corridor (near Location 2): older buildings, affordable, high foot traffic, Jamaican/Caribbean + South Asian + European mix.
- Bramalea: South Asian dominant, Caribbean mix, budget-conscious families, strong community feel.
- Gore Meadows: newest development, new immigrant families, fast growing.

## Consumer Psychology Notes
- Word-of-mouth and community WhatsApp/Facebook groups drive decisions more than ads.
- Food = cultural identity for 1st/2nd gen immigrants. A brand that "gets their culture" earns loyalty.

# Cultural Calendar & Campaign Hooks (Brampton)

| Month | Occasion | Target Community | Campaign Idea | Hero Dish |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| April | Vaisakhi (Sikh New Year) | Punjabi Sikh, 163K in Brampton | Family feast package, Punjabi-language caption | Chicken Skewers + Lamb Seekh |
| May/Jun | Eid ul-Fitr | Muslim community, 20,400+ | Family bundle offer, clean meat messaging front and centre | Biryani + Chicken Sajji |
| Jun/Jul | Eid ul-Adha (Bakra Eid) | Muslim community, lamb-forward | Lamb week campaign, "the lamb you've been waiting for" | Lamb Chops + Lamb Seekh |
| Jul/Aug | Caribbean Carnival / JAMBANA | Jamaican + Caribbean, 40K+ | Bold sauces, BBQ wraps, Doner focus, Clarence St hero content | Doner + Smoked Chicken Wrap |
| Sep/Oct | Navratri | Gujarati Hindu families | Vegetarian spotlight week, Paneer Tikka as hero | Paneer Tikka + Grilled Veg |
| Oct/Nov | Diwali | Hindu + Sikh, largest South Asian occasion | Diwali family feast, premium platter, warm golden

title: 05-cultural-calendar-campaigns (part 2)
text:
eg |
| Oct/Nov | Diwali | Hindu + Sikh, largest South Asian occasion | Diwali family feast, premium platter, warm golden visuals | Full menu, family platter |
| Nov | Guru Nanak Gurpurab | Sikh community | Community gratitude post, no hard sell | Chicken Seekh Kabab |
| Dec | Christmas/New Year | Filipino Catholic + Caribbean | Holiday feast campaign, dessert upsell | Sajji + Dessert selection |

## Quarterly Themes
- Q2 (Apr-Jun): Vaisakhi, Ramadan tail-end, Eid ul-Fitr
- Q3 (Jul-Sep): Summer BBQ, Caribbean Carnival, patio season content
- Q4 (Oct-Dec): Navratri, Diwali, Gurpurab, Christmas/New Year

## Rule
Plan campaign content at least 2 weeks before each occasion. These are the highest-revenue windows
of the year and are treated as the backbone of the content calendar, not optional add-ons.

# Content & Social Media Strategy

## Six Content Pillars
1. We Respect Every Table - no pork, no beef, no alcohol, clean meat, every culture welcomed
2. Your Culture, Your Plate - Sajji = Balochi, Biryani = South Asian comfort, Doner = Mediterranean
3. Build Your Own Plate - protein + sauce + side, vegan/GF builds
4. Real Flame. Not Overpriced. - grill visuals, "others charge $40+, we don't," honest pricing story
5. Live Grill Experience - fire/smoke close-ups, char marks forming, raw-to-plated in 60 seconds
6. Speed + Brampton Community - two locations, cultural occasions, family Friday posts

## Weekly Posting Rhythm
- Monday 12-1pm: Photo/Carousel - Pillar 1 or 2 (cultural respect / clean meat messaging)
- Wednesday 6-8pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 4 or 5 (grill footage / price hook)
- Friday 5-7pm: Photo/Carousel - Pillar 3 or 4 (build your plate / family occasion)
- Sunday 6-9pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 2 or 6 (brand story / community)

Content formula: 1 confirmed strength +

- Sunday 6-9pm: Reel/Short Video - Pillar 2 or 6 (brand story / community)

Content formula: 1 confirmed strength + 1 menu item per week.
All platforms get the same video simultaneously.
Ads always launch/reset on Tuesdays.

## Visual Rules for Every Post
- Dark, near-black background, food should pop
- Warm amber/gold flame-toned lighting, never cool/clinical
- Always show char marks, sauce drizzle, steam, or cut interior
- Lazzat logo subtle in a bottom corner of every image
- Video always vertical 9:16, always with subtitles (sound-off viewing must work)

## Growth Tactics
- Bill-time follow-and-review discount
- Reel-based coupon codes, extendable to Uber Eats/DoorDash
- Hot sauce challenge
- Dedicated content creator team model
- Weekly review contest
- Trending audio and keyword capture, adopt new platform features early

## Influencer Approach
Direct local Brampton micro-influencer outreach works better than platform-based outreach
(platforms like Collabstr mainly yielded

text:

(platforms like Collabstr mainly yielded paid-collab requests, not organic fits).
Process: personal DM, no script, complimentary tasting for two, ask to add @lazzat.ca as collaborator
on their reel. Soha handles on-ground hospitality when Usama is remote. Follow-up via WhatsApp.
No cash payment in early phase, food only.

## Opening Special (reference)
50% off Sajji full chicken at $18.99. Redemption requires customer to tag Lazzat Instagram in-store
and leave a Google review.

## GMB Review System
1. Verbal ask from staff to every satisfied customer
2. QR code review card in every bag
3. WhatsApp follow-up 1 hour after pickup
Respond to every review (positive and negative) within 24 hours.
Target: 10 reviews week 1, 25 by week 2, 50 by month 1.

Increase visibility in local takeaway searches in Brampton, bring more traffic, more orders.

## Blog Plan
2 blogs per week. Each targets a local Brampton keyword cluster.
Every blog must include: a local reference (Brampton, McVean Dr, Clarence St), an FAQ section for
featured snippet eligibility, internal links to menu/ordering pages, optimized image alt text.

Priority blog topics (from planning docs):

5. Best Biryani Takeaway in Brampton (best biryani Brampton)

- Image alt text describes the dish + location, not generic filenames

- Citation building: Yelp, TripAdvisor, Zomato, Yellow Pages, local directories

## Google My Business (GMB)
- Category: Takeout Restaurant (primary)
- Complete all fields: hours per location, attributes (No Alcohol, Vegetarian/Vegan Options, Parking, WiFi)

- Review acquisition is priority #1 in first two weeks (see content-social-strategy file)

- Phase 1: Top 100 results - basic SEO + blog publishing
- Phase 2: Top 10 (first page) - internal linking, technical SEO, some backlinks

# Competitor Intelligence (Clarence St Area)

## The Single Biggest Finding
After analyzing 26+ competitors near Clarence St: zero restaurants combine Charcoal/Lava Grill +
No Pork/Beef/Alcohol + Global Menu + All Delivery Platforms + Active Social Media.
Lazzat owns this lane by default.

## Direct Competitors
### King Tandoori Kennedy
4.0 stars, 7,757+ reviews, 8,137 IG followers. Open 24 hours.
Weakness: HAS FULL ALCOHOL BAR, not halal. Portions shrinking. Plastic found in food (documented).
Lazzat angle: "Every item clean. No alcohol. No confusion."

### Baigs Grill
4.2 stars, 2,047 reviews, 1,192 IG (only 49 posts).
Weakness: Closed Monday AND Tuesday. $452 bad bill complaint. Biryani "tasteless, missing meat." Zero TikTok.
Lazzat angle: Post "WE ARE OPEN" every Mon/Tue. Target disappointed biryani customers.

### Sharmz Mediterranean
4.6 stars, 524 reviews, 324 IG followers despite 413 posts. Zero delivery apps.
Weakness: massive content effort, near-zero return, unreachable by

Weakness: massive content effort, near-zero return, unreachable by delivery customers.
Lazzat angle: capture their entire delivery-only customer base automatically.

### Caravan Kabob House
4.2 stars, 1,509 reviews. Afghani cuisine.
Weakness: caterpillars found in salad (GMB screenshot). Zero social media presence at all.
Lazzat angle: "Open kitchen. Clean flame. You see every dish made."

## Partial/Overlap Competitors (watch list)
- Paranthe Wali Gali (same building as Clarence St): closed Tuesday, hair in food complaint, greasy reviews
- Blackstone Steakhouse: $50-90/person, no delivery, 4,622 IG followers but only 13 posts
- Patty Kulcha: kulcha only, narrow menu, viral TikTok formula worth studying
- Osmow's Shawarma: chain, inconsistent quality, undercooked rice complaints
- Lazeez Shawarma: shrinkflation complaints, rude staff complaints

## Indirect / Monitor Only
Village of India (3.8 stars, greasy buffet), Nepali Momo

## Indirect / Monitor Only

(plastic in food), Jamaica House Jerk (zero social media despite 1,039 reviews), Pizza Pros (2.8 stars,
lowest in the area, hygiene issues).

## Recurring Competitor Failure Patterns (use as Lazzat service standard bar)
- Hair in food: documented across 4+ competitors
- Plastic/foreign objects in food: 2 documented cases
- Shrinking portions / shrinkflation complaints: multiple chains
- Zero or weak TikTok presence across almost all competitors
- Several competitors closed 1-2 days per week, losing consistent weekly revenue
- Several competitors have zero delivery app presence at all

## Strategic Takeaways for Lazzat
1. Halal/Clean trust: be the loudest, clearest "clean meat, no alcohol" brand in the area
2. Social media: post consistently, most competitors have failed here badly
3. Delivery apps: be live on all three (Uber

Lazzat launched April 26, 2026.

## Active Workstreams
- Influencer marketing: direct local Brampton micro-influencer outreach (platform outreach was dropped, yielded mostly paid-collab requests). Complimentary tastings, Soha handles on-ground hospitality, @lazzat.ca added as collaborator on reels, follow-up via WhatsApp.
- Social growth: bill-time follow-and-review discount, reel-based coupon codes (extending to delivery apps), hot sauce challenge, content creator team model, weekly review contest.
- Opening special: 50% off Sajji full chicken at $18.99, requires Instagram tag + Google review.
- Packaging procurement: via Alibaba, contact Iris. Unit 13 warehouse address issue: newly built, postal code not recognized in some logistics databases, needs manual entry.

1. **Fresh First** — real ingredients, never shortcuts
2. **Fire Makes Flavor** — live flame and patience matter

### Dr. Preservo Rules

- Operatic ham, always foiled, never scary
- Can learn one small helpful thing in Year-3 finale

## AI Video Pipeline (Standard)

1. Define product/scene and final length
2. Create consistent keyframes in one visual world
3. Generate short AI clips between adjacent keyframes (or image-to-video with orbit motion)
4. Stitch in CapCut + text/music/SFX
5. Log prompts in `Lazzat_AI_Video_Generation_Log.csv`

### Models (Magnific)
| Task | Model |
|------|-------|
| Image frames | `imagen-nano-banana-2` (quality) or `-flash` (draft) |
| Video (realistic) | `bytedance-seedance-pro-2.0` or `kling-21-master` |
| Orbit/camera motion | `kling-21-master`, 1:1, 1080p, 10s |
| Menu board motion | Kling 2.5 start→end keyframes (**never ffmpeg zoompan**) |

### Prompting Rules
- ✅ natural premium food commercial, warm studio lighting, macro lens, shallow DOF, locked subject
- ❌ changing plates/product shape, logo distortion, random backgrounds, distorted hands, face drift
